title: How innovative is India?
standfirst: India is 38th of 139 economies in WIPO's Global Innovation Index 2026, up from 81st in 2015. That rank captures real strengths, misses others, and rests partly on changes in what the index counts. Here is what is inside it, checked against India's own data on research and patents.

short.headline: India ranks 38th of 139 on innovation, far better than its income predicts
short.dek: India has climbed from the bottom half of the Global Innovation Index to its top third since 2015. The strength is in outputs and scale; the weakness is per person.
short.body: India is 38th of 139 in the Global Innovation Index 2026, with an audited range of 34th to 39th. It scores about 13.5 points above what its income predicts, the eighth-largest margin in the index, and higher than 33 of 35 upper-middle-income economies. Three-quarters of its lead over a typical economy comes from outputs: IT services exports, where it ranks first, unicorn valuations and patents, where filings have risen fivefold since 2016-17, most of them now from universities. On inputs per person it is weak: 259 researchers per million people in 2020 (354 on DST's newer survey) and R&D spending of 0.65 to 0.84 per cent of GDP, against a world average of 2.6. Part of the climb from 81st in 2015 reflects changes in the index itself.

macha.heading: Tell me what this means, bro
macha.body: India is good at innovation for a country of its income, and it is big, so its totals look impressive: third in the world for scientific papers, fifth for patent filings, second for IT services exports. Divide by 146 crore people and most of those numbers drop to somewhere between 38th and 89th. And most of the recent patent jump comes from universities, whose applications also count towards rankings and accreditation.
macha.soWhat: When you see India's innovation rank in a headline, ask two things: per person or in total, and which part of the index moved. The number that would tell you India is becoming inventive across the board is researchers per million people: 259 in 2020 on UNESCO's count, 354 in 2023-24 on DST's wider new survey, against about 1,650 for the world.

caveats: WIPO states that Global Innovation Index scores and ranks are not directly comparable between editions, because indicators, data and the set of economies change. No consistent back-series exists.

In 2023 WIPO replaced new businesses per person (India 114th) with unicorn valuation (India 9th) in the knowledge and technology outputs pillar; most of India's rise on that pillar since 2022 came in that edition.

Ranks are shown as the share of other ranked economies India is ahead of, so that editions covering 125 to 143 economies can share one axis. The shaded band is the Joint Research Centre's 90 per cent interval, published from 2012.

India's R&D spending and researcher figures in the 2026 index describe 2020. DST's newer figures (to 2023-24) come from a new national survey with wider coverage and are not comparable with earlier years.
Two of India's best eleven indicator ranks, on finance for startups and on entrepreneurship policy, come from expert-opinion surveys by the Global Entrepreneurship Monitor, not from counted data.

Educational institutions became a separate patent-fee category on 21 September 2021. Earlier university filings are inside 'other than natural persons'. A patent application is not a granted patent, and grants by applicant type are not published.
State patent counts follow the applicant's address. Per-person figures use the National Commission on Population's projections interpolated to 1 March 2025, as India has had no census since 2011.
WIPO's cluster method changed in 2023 and again in 2025; only the 2025 and 2026 cluster ranks are comparable.
Total and per-person ranks compare each economy's latest available year since 2018 or 2020, so years differ between countries.
The index barely sees diffusion of existing technology within firms, informal and grassroots innovation, or the quality and commercial value of patents.
